findings.title: Task 2 says the suite passes "unchanged", but an existing test pins the full metric set
findings.description: Task 2 changes `PythonAdapter.metrics` (now `frozenset(SnapshotMetric)` at `src/squadron/metrology/snapshot/python_adapter.py:105`) to the four 400 metrics. Its success line is "the full `tests/metrology/` suite passes unchanged". But `test_adapter_declares_its_metrics_and_pb2_conventions` asserts `adapter.metrics == set(SnapshotMetric)`. Once the enum grows and the set narrows, that test fails, so the success line can't be met and the Task 2 commit isn't at a passing point. Tasks 8 and 12 change the set again, and Task 25 brings it back to the full set. Fix: in Task 2, change this assertion to the explicit four-metric set. Each later task that adds a metric then updates the same assertion. Change the success line to "passes, with only that assertion edited".

findings.title: Task 14 makes `MemoryError` a per-file token error, which contradicts D3 and Task 11
findings.description: D3, the failure-mode table, Task 10 (line 123) and Task 11 (line 139) all say a `MemoryError` during the duplication pass makes `duplicated_lines` `tool_failed`. It must never be a partial figure. Task 14 lists `MemoryError` in TypeScript's `token_errors`. Task 10 (line 121) says those errors put the file in `unparsed_files` with a WARNING. So for TypeScript, an out-of-memory condition would quietly drop one file and still report a duplication count. That is the partial figure D3 forbids, and which branch wins depends on the order of the `except` clauses. 400 does list `MemoryError` as a length parse error (`src/squadron/metrology/snapshot/typescript_length.py:151`), which explains where this came from, but D3 sets a different rule for duplication. Fix: Task 14 should pass only `TypeScriptParseError` as the token error. Task 10 should state that `MemoryError` is always caught at pass level, ahead of `token_errors`.

findings.title: Commit markers are checkboxes, not `**Commit**:` lines
findings.description: Every commit point is written as `- [ ] Commit: …` (lines 46, 68, 88, 97, 115, 142, 156, 171, 183, 191, 208, 229, 246, 262, 271, 276, 283, 290). The project rule says implementation commits happen only at `**Commit**:` markers, and those markers are plain lines, never checkboxes. Under that rule, this file has no recognised markers. That falls back to "commit at the end of each top-level task", which would commit after untested implementation tasks (3, 5, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 19, 21, 23, 25). A checkbox commit also has to be ticked after the commit itself, so the tick lands in a separate checkbox-only commit, which the rules forbid. The placement is otherwise right: every marker sits after a test task or at a verified point. Fix: change each one to a plain `**Commit**: …` line, keeping the same positions.

findings.title: SC10's "other metrics unchanged" isn't asserted at adapter level
findings.description: Task 11 tests the token ceiling only through `measure_duplication` alone. SC10, and the failure-mode table's outcome column (which the Technical Requirements say tests must assert), also require the language's other metrics to stay present. One extra check in Task 13 would cover it: lower `DUPLICATION_MAX_TOKENS` and confirm that `file_length`, `function_length` and `cyclomatic_complexity` are still present.

findings.title: Task 9's `RecursionError` case doesn't check the WARNING
findings.description: In the failure-mode table, the `RecursionError` row has the signal "WARNING per file". The Technical Requirements ask tests to check both the signal and the outcome, but Task 9 checks only that the file lands in `unparsed_files`. Add a check for the warning.

findings.title: Every success criterion has a task
findings.description:
- SC1: Tasks 8–9, 12–15, 26
- SC2: Task 9
- SC3: Tasks 4, 6
- SC4: Tasks 11, 13, 15
- SC5: Tasks 22, 26
- SC6: Tasks 20, 24, and walkthrough step 4
- SC7: Tasks 20, 24, and walkthrough step 9
- SC8: Tasks 20, 24
- SC9: Task 17
- SC10: Task 11
- SC11: Task 26
- SC12: Task 7

Technical requirements: real fixtures (Task 18), module size limits (Task 30). Integration requirements: the contract freeze (Task 30) and the docs (Task 28). The walkthrough is Task 29. No task falls outside the slice's scope.

findings.title: Sequencing and test placement
findings.description:
- The order follows the slice's Development Approach.
- Every dependency comes first: the Task 7 read helper before Task 10, Task 16's parser before Task 21, and the Task 18 fixtures before Task 20.
- Every test task comes straight after its implementation task, and there are no circular dependencies.
- Before Task 27, `render.py`'s generic fallback (`src/squadron/metrology/snapshot/render.py:54-63`) handles the new metrics, so the full suite stays green in between.

findings.title: Size fits the slice; no load test needed
findings.description: The slice has 30 tasks in one file. That fits four metrics across three subsystems in two languages, and each task is small enough to finish on its own. The slice states no NFR; the token ceiling is a design limit, tested by lowering the constant. So no `tests/load/` task or CI gating is required.
